# T7.00 (part): naming our VideoToolbox encoders

> The full "why no third party can register a VideoToolbox encoder system-wide" write-up (bundle signing, MediaExtension
> being decode-only, the decoder dead-end, the CLI injection route, the Feedback angle) is in `T7.00-cli-and-extensions.md`.

Apps listed ours as "Dynamically Registered avc1/hvc1 Video Encoder". Now (user's format, 2026-10-18):
**"NVENC - H.264 - (NVIDIA RTX 4090) - mickys/nvenc - 0.7.0"** and **"NVENC - HEVC - (NVIDIA RTX 4090) - mickys/nvenc - 0.7.0"**:
the card from the GPU's IORegistry `model` ("NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090" minus "NVIDIA " / "GeForce "), the version from
`git describe --tags --always --dirty` at build time (`build.sh` -> `NVENC_VERSION`; tags `vX.Y.Z`, v0.7.0 = M7). Shown by
VTCopyVideoEncoderList and OBS's encoder menus; the derived alpha encoder gets "Apple Muxed Alpha-" in front. Command-line apps that never create a Metal device still can't see the encoder
at all; that half of T7.00 stays open.

## How it was found (2026-10-18)

Sources: a public decompile of iOS 26.1's VideoToolbox and CoreMedia (GitHub `EthanArbuckle/iPhone18-3_26.1_23B85_Restore`,
found by searching GitHub for the "Dynamically Registered" string), and macOS 26.7.1's own code read in-process
(`fnmap`: calls resolved with dladdr, stubs followed, CFString/C-string references printed; byte dumps disassembled with
objdump on the dev VM; no debugger, which needs developer mode).

1. **`VTRegisterVideoEncoderWithInfo`** builds the name itself (`"Dynamically Registered %@ Video Encoder"`) and passes
   it to `vtRegisterVideoEncoderInternal`, which writes it as `VTEncoderName` into the registry entry. Nothing in our info
   dictionary can change it (13 key shapes tried; only the ID and `VTRating` are read).
2. **Plug-in bundles** carry `VTEncoderName` in their `Info.plist` (`CMClassImplementations`), and VideoToolbox scans
   `/System/Library/Video/Plug-Ins` and `/Library/Video/Plug-Ins` (plus two `/AppleInternal` folders). A test bundle in
   `/Library/Video/Plug-Ins` *is* scanned and cached by CoreMedia, but VideoToolbox adds every search path with option
   bit 0 set (`options = 1 + 2a + 8b`), and CoreMedia's `figRegistryAddResultItem` then checks each bundle against
   `kFigRegistryAppleCodeSignRequirement`:
   `anchor apple or anchor apple generic and info[CFBundleIdentifier] = "com.apple."* and certificate leaf[field.1.2.840.113635.100.6.1.9] or … leaf[field.1.2.840.113635.100.6.1.27]`.
   Only Apple can sign a bundle that passes. `VTRegisterVideoEncoderBundleDirectory(CFURL)` only accepts folders under
   `/System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/` or inside a bundle signed like the app's main bundle. The pro-workflow folder
   needs the app to call `VTRegisterProfessionalVideoWorkflowVideoEncoders` and is subject to the same check.
3. **The registry entry's description is mutable** (`__NSDictionaryM`, the same object `FigRegistryItemCopyDescription`
   returns), and VideoToolbox reads `VTEncoderName` / `VTCodecName` from it every time it lists encoders.

## What libnvencvt does now

After registering, `rename_encoders()`:
- finds VideoToolbox's encoder registry: a pointer in VideoToolbox's writable `__DATA*` sections to a live heap object
  whose isa and CF type ID match a `FigRegistry` (learnt from one we create) and whose class field is
  `com.apple.videotoolbox.videoencoder` (no instruction decoding, so it does not depend on code layout);
- lists its items (`FigRegistryCopyFilteredItemList`, `FigRegistryItemCopyDescription`, exported by CoreMedia), and for
  our two IDs sets `VTEncoderName` and `VTCodecName` ("H.264" / "HEVC"), **only if** the dictionary is `__NSDictionaryM`
  (mutable; `_CFDictionaryIsMutable` says 0 for every dictionary on macOS 26) and still holds the default
  "Dynamically Registered…" name. Anything unexpected leaves the default name. `NVENCVT_NO_RENAME=1` turns it off.
- Cost: ~0.3 ms (register + rename ~1 ms in a GUI-like process).

Checked: vttest (encoders listed with the new names, encodes unchanged), OBS 32.2.2 (log and the Output > Video
Encoder menu show "nvenc H.264 (NVIDIA RTX 40)"; recording through it decodes clean).
